brief.headline: Cut the ₹28.69 L/yr extra we pay above our cheapest supplier — we're 47.43% of their revenue and have five credible alternates lined up.

priceAsk.summary: Match the prices Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic give us on the three biggest items — or close to market fair bands for the 28 mm cap.
priceAsk.target: ₹28.69 L/yr saving by moving to our best prices: 28 mm cap from ₹1.08 to ₹0.81 (Mars Plastics), 30 ml bottle from ₹1.53 to ₹1.38 (Mars Plastics), measuring cup from ₹0.46 to ₹0.35 (Premier Plastic)
priceAsk.basis: We already pay those lower prices to other suppliers for the same packaging — those are real, not hypothetical. The 28 mm cap sits in the ₹0.55–1.20/pc market asking band, verdict says fair with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume, so our target of ₹0.81 is justified and leaves them margin.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 45 days — we won't push for longer payment, but if they want faster (say 30 days), trade it for a 4–5% price cut on the big items.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Keeping 45 days costs us nothing extra. Moving to 30 days would free up ₹16.02 L for us, but only if we get a matching discount to make it worth our while.

brief.financialLeverage: They're small (₹4.11 Cr revenue) and we're huge to them — our ₹1.95 Cr is 47.43% of everything they sell, so losing us would be a serious hit. They keep only 6.0% of every ₹100 they sell, while similar firms keep 15.0%, meaning price cuts squeeze them harder. They owe 1.13× their own cash (₹1.95 Cr debt) and their cash is tied up for 101 days (a bit better than the 107 day peer norm, but still long), so cash is a bit tight and they borrow at about 4.54%–8%. Their books put them in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.83), flagged as a small entity to verify, and free cash flow is negative (₹-79.14 L). All that means: push firmly on price because we have real alternates and they can't afford to lose us, but don't squeeze so hard you tip a fragile supplier — focus the ask on matching our best prices, not on brutal cuts below market.

evidence.point: We pay ₹28.69 L/yr extra versus the lowest prices we already get from other suppliers
On the 28 mm PP cap alone, we pay ₹1.08/NOS; Mars Plastics gives us ₹0.81/NOS — a 33.2% gap costing us ₹14.05 L/yr
We are 47.43% of their total revenue — our ₹1.95 Cr spend against their ₹4.11 Cr sales
They keep 6.0% profit, well below the 15.0% that similar firms earn
They owe 1.13× their own cash (₹1.95 Cr debt) and their Altman Z score is 1.83 (grey zone)
Market asking band for 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict says fair with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, pharma bottles and caps specialist, revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health score B (65/100) — top second-source candidate, much stronger than Cincorp.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma packaging — robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging supplier, broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: They're in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.83) with negative free cash flow (₹-79.14 L) and flagged as a small entity — don't push so hard you destabilise supply; line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a qualified backup before you go aggressive.

We're 47.43% of their revenue — if we move volume out suddenly, it could hurt them badly and leave us scrambling; phase any switch carefully or negotiate a phased price step-down to keep supply stable.

They keep only 6.0% profit (vs 15.0% peers) — big price cuts may not stick if they can't deliver profitably; focus the ask on matching our best prices (which are real and sustainable), not on squeezing below market.

They already pay their own suppliers in 39 days (vs 23 day peer median) — they're stretching cash themselves, so demanding longer payment terms (beyond 45 days) won't fly and could strain the relationship; keep payment where it is unless you trade faster payment for a discount.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more per year than the prices Mars and Premier give us for identical packaging — let's talk about how we close that gap and keep the business with you.
